title: Readers send a message through a public contact form; it lands in newsroom Messages
description:
As a reader of a Papyrus publication, I can send the editors a message (corrections, tips, questions) from a contact form on the public site, and editors see it in the newsroom's Messages as a reader message they can triage and reply to by email.

Shares the public-endpoint work of this milestone (newsletter signup): an unauthenticated, rate-limited endpoint with a bot challenge (e.g. Turnstile) and a honeypot, strict size limits, no reflection of input, and an explicit consent line. Stores a Message (messageKind reader_contact; name, reply-to email, topic, body, page URL, received-at) in the site backend, visible to editors and admins only, never through the guest or content API; email addresses are personal data (same handling as subscriber records). Optional notification to editors (e.g. Slack or email) when one arrives.

Site contract: the publication's static site renders a /contact/ page whose form posts to a configured endpoint; while the endpoint is not configured the page says the form is not open yet and never fakes a successful send. Pilot: Distinctive Mark (its editorial policy points readers to the footer contact link for corrections). Acceptance: a message sent from the live form appears in Messages within seconds; spam controls block scripted posts; editors can mark handled and reply.
